note: No rule of the Central Bank of Solomon Islands fixing an account number's length was read. ANZ's Solomon Islands branch, in its page and Quick Reference Guide on the Central Bank's national payment system upgrade under the National Payment System Act 2022 (from 8 April 2024; read 2026-10-30, the guide dated 4/24), gives each receiving bank's account number, the bank named by its SWIFT code beside the number (replacing the ACH codes SI01 to SI06): ANZ seven digits, which can be between four and seven; BSP nine or ten; Bred Bank fifteen; Pan Oceanic Bank twelve (shorter ones padded with zeros at the front); the Central Bank five. So the number is written as four to fifteen digits, drawn at nine or ten, BSP's, the bank the game's Solomon Islands account is held at (BSP Solomon Islands); that is ANZ's statement of BSP's numbers, not BSP's own, a reading to check. No check digit is published, and the bank isn't coded inside the number.
